name: Adela Griffin
life: “I still remember an evening announcer who always sounded forgiving.” On Saturday, near Maré Coffee, Adela likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I never learned the stations' names. I memorized how far the dial turned from the crack.
appearance: Out of work clothes, look for a red windbreaker and a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. Adela has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, with steel-colored hair cut square above the collar. Adela grins on one side while the eyes stay serious during a conversation.
personality: Adela has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To mark the favorite station position for the next listener.
family: Gregory Lang is Adela’s cousin. Adela picks the meeting place. Gregory sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *An ordinary mirror*, Gregory says, “I own the mirror and have seen a hundred other lives in it.”
connections: Lisa Anders. The wheel that needn't work can keep the position remembered by touch.

reactions.response: Adela checks the repair bench before assuming anyone took the dial.
